thread:
ashley: Seeing a tail latency blip on prod since ~02:30 UTC, only affects a handful of tenants.  p95 -> p99 jump from ~80ms to ~520ms for text-generation route. Not across the board but repeatable when we run a 10qps steady load against model:gpt-small-quant.

matt: hmm did we just push the admission control tweak yesterday?  I remember toggling the microbatch growth cap in the scheduler service.

ashley: yes rolled at 01:45 UTC. Change was: allow microbatch size to grow to 32 if queueing. Before we capped at 16. I can revert but want to understand root cause first.

ciara: uploading a quick trace and a sampled CPU profile from the affected host: https://perf.internal/runs/216234-ashley-trace

perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flamegraphs/216234-0825 (size ~2.3MB)

bryan: quick guess: larger microbatches are interacting with KV cache eviction policy. If KV cache misses spike, we fall back to kernel variant that pulls keys from CPU/PCI which kills tail latency.

ashley: logs from one affected worker (trimmed):
```
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z INFO admit: batch_size=28 tenant=acme queue_ms=12
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z WARN kv: miss_rate=0.67 shard=3
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z INFO kernel: selected=fused_fp16_batched latency_ms=480
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z INFO kvcache: evicted=1024 reason=hotspot
```

matt: that kvcache miss_rate is wild. Could be a tenant hot-shard. Do we have per-tenant KV hit heatmaps? ciara, can you pull per-tenant cache stats and kernel-selection counts over the window?

ciara: pulled and attached small table (summarized): tenant acme shows kvcache hit 28% during spike, others at 92%. Kernel selector flips to 'fused_fp16_batched' more often for acme because kv misses cause longer seq recompute. Also noticed increased memcpy time in the profile.

bryan: memcpy indicates fallback path to host memory or small-kernel that requires extra copies. That explains p99. Microbatching increases the amount of in-flight KV keys and amplifies eviction pressure.

ashley: repro plan: run a 10qps steady load against acme tenant on canary cluster with microbatch cap=16 vs 32. If cap=16 stays healthy -> rollback is safe. Scheduling a controlled test now.

matt: also try temporarily pinning kernel selector to 'streaming_fp16' for the canary to see if kernel choice mitigates latency (run with --force-kernel). If that lowers p99, then kernel-selection fallback path is a big contributor.

ciara: test results:
- cap=32: p95=95ms p99=510ms throughput stable
- cap=16: p95=88ms p99=92ms
- cap=32 + --force-kernel=streaming_fp16: p95=90ms p99=130ms

ashley: thanks. Looks like two factors: (1) larger microbatches increase KV working set causing hotspot evictions, (2) evictions trigger kernel fallback that does extra memcpy and stalls. Rolling back cap to 16 now and opening follow-up to address kvcache eviction heuristics and kernel selector resilience.

bryan: agree. Action items:
- rollback microbatch cap (ashley) ✅ in progress
- add eviction backpressure: throttle admission when miss-rate > 40% (matt)
- make kernel selector prefer streaming variant if kvcache miss-rate high (ciara)
- add per-tenant hot-shard alerts (ashley + infra)

ashley: rollback applied at 02:47 UTC, p99 dropped back to ~95ms on affected tenants. Creating an incident PR and will coordinate a patch for eviction/backpressure.

perf-bot: incident created: INC-2026-314 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-314)
